summary.headline: Q2 FY27 pre-sales rose 83% YoY to INR470 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR107 crore at a 39.9% margin.
summary.overview: Management reported strong Q2 and H1 FY27 growth in pre-sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with margins above 38%. Three redevelopment projects were added in the quarter, adding an estimated INR2,700-2,800 crore GDV, taking the pipeline to 24 projects and about INR20,000 crore GDV. Collections were weaker at INR60 crore in Q2 and INR209 crore in H1, which management attributed to construction-linked billing and expects to improve in H2. Analysts focused on collections, the INR300 crore business development outflow, Prabhadevi sales traction and project timeline slippage.

segments.name: Lotus Trident (Andheri West, luxury commercial)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR178 crore pre-sales in its first full quarter after end-June launch, about 35% of sales sold within three months per management. Management guided EBITDA margin of 33-35%.

segments.name: Residential luxury projects
segments.commentary: Celestia reported 36% sales within six months of launch. Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi) reported healthy inquiries, but Lotus Prabhadevi (GDV ~INR800 crore) contributed no pre-sales in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance reiterated at INR1,800-2,000 crore.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guided at 55-60% over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 35-40% and PAT margin at 25-30%.
Four H2 FY27 launches planned: Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino and Lotus Odyssey, combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore; about 90% approvals in place.
Project-level surplus estimated at about INR9,500 crore over the development cycle; projects expected to complete over the next 4-4.5 years.
Management expects H2 collections to be much better than H1 as projects reach plinth level; FY28 collection guidance to be given at the start of FY28.
Amara and Athena expected to receive OC in FY27 (Amara within the quarter or by March; Athena before March).
capex_capacity: Pipeline of 24 ongoing and upcoming projects, aggregate GDV ~INR20,000 crore, of which 19 are redevelopment-led.
Business development: Lotus Impressa (Shivaji Park, Dadar West), Lotus Stellar (Versova) and Lotus Supremus (Juhu) added in Q2.
INR550 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for subsidiary (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun); INR305 crore deployed as of 30 Sep 2026 of INR732 crore net proceeds.
Upfront premium paid to government for new projects in Q2, which management said is to save costs and secure supplier discounts; new projects typically need 8-10% of project cost to start.
GIFT City plot of 5.5 acres on Sabarmati riverfront; expected 1.3-1.5 million sq ft mixed-use development subject to town planning scheme approval.
Lotus Monarch timeline pushed out by one year due to society, trust, Charity Commissioner and government approvals; Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended.
demand_pricing: Management says the luxury segment is less sensitive to RBI's 25 bps repo hike to 5.5% (first hike since early 2023); buyers rely less on home loans.
Mumbai H1 CY2026 sales of homes priced above INR10 crore reached a record INR18,500 crore; prime residential prices up 6.2% YoY per management.
Management says prices have risen across almost all projects in H1 and will rise further as construction progresses if the market supports it.
Management says it is the only suburban player to have completed a commercial redevelopment (Arc One), and has 2-3 more commercial redevelopment projects; about five commercial projects in portfolio.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria) pricing set at a premium, with 270-degree sea view and ~200 m Art Deco tower; management says no pushback, pre-sales expected to show in next two quarters.
Collections as a share of pre-sales: management said completion-stage projects carry 90-95% balance due, and expects 95-100% collection on three projects completing next year.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins above 35% during expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited net debt-free status (no interest burden), minimal marketing spend, a 2.5-3.5 year project cycle that speeds fund deployment, and premium pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for Trident and what is the commercial redevelopment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided Trident EBITDA margin at 33-35%, in line with guidance. Management expects commercial redevelopment to carry sustainable margins and cited 2-3 more projects.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections catch up with pre-sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said collections are construction-linked: about 5-10% at launch and about 25% at plinth. Of about INR800 crore H1 pre-sales, INR200 crore was collected, and H2 should improve as two of three recent projects move past basement.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gives annual guidance only. It pointed to ~INR20,000 crore GDV and ~INR9,500 crore project surplus, with completion over the next 4-4.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did timelines shift for upcoming projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Monarch moved out by one year due to multiple approving bodies. Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended. Management says overall guidance is unchanged and new projects will replace slipped ones.

qa_highlights.question: Why no Prabhadevi pre-sales, and will the business development outflow constrain the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Prabhadevi is a new micromarket with marketing under way and results expected in two quarters. The INR300 crore outflow was upfront government fees and discounted supplier payments; management said cash is sufficient. Operating cash flow will stay negative in launch periods, though Arcadian is working-capital positive.

risks_watch: Collections lag: Q2 collections of INR60 crore and H1 of INR209 crore against H1 pre-sales of about INR800-879 crore; track whether H2 collections rise as two of three recent projects move past basement to plinth.

Timeline slippage: Lotus Monarch pushed out by one year (society, trust, Charity Commissioner, government approvals) and Ghatkopar (Salona) extended; watch whether replacement projects keep FY27 guidance intact.

Cash deployment: INR305 crore of INR732 crore IPO net proceeds deployed by 30 Sep 2026; management says operating cash flow may stay negative in launch periods, with no FY28 collection guidance until start of FY28.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria, GDV ~INR800 crore) had no Q2 pre-sales; management expects results in next two quarters at a premium price point.
Delivery of four H2 FY27 launches (combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore, about 90% approvals) and the FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crore versus H1 INR879 crore.
key_quotes: Delighted to share that we recorded pre-sales for the quarter at INR470 crores, up 83% year-on-year.
Collections in our business are linked to construction milestones and can vary from quarter -to-quarter.
So, right now, it's not a good time to because we need to evaluate and update you.
So, project-wise, yes, but overall, maybe we cannot give that.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sales, margins and launch plans, with the CEO and CFO more cautious and non-committal on collection timing, FY28 numbers and operating cash flow, deferring to the start of FY28 or project-level answers. Management repeatedly stressed the net debt-free balance sheet and construction-linked billing as the reason collections trail pre-sales.
